readall_conflicts: No disagreement between sources about Coast Miwok: the only listed open-copy work (Golla 2011) says nothing about Coast Miwok or Miwok-family stress, and the older open sources already held by the project (Kroeber 1911, Barrett 1908, Wikipedia, WALS, Glottolog) are likewise silent for coas1301 (Kroeber's accent remarks concern Northern and Southern Sierra Miwok only). One correction to a sibling record: lists Golla's 'Stress is not distinctive' sentence under Miwok; chaining the fragment forward shows it is the Tubatulabal paragraph (absolute suffixes -l/-t, hani:-ni?in 'my house' vs hani:-l 'the house'), so it must not be used as a Miwok or Coast Miwok statement.

tone.quote: I have not written accents on the words -- these can be found in the dictionary if desired. Callaghan writes a number of unaccented grammatical particles (notably ka, indicating past tense) as either ka or kaa. There is no discernible grammatical difference between these two forms (as opposed to accented káa, which she (and I) always write with long /a/). ... In summary, I do not present any new phonological, morphological or lexicological analysis here of Callaghan's and Applegate’s elicited data

tone.quote: Concerning the orthography, c is pronounced as English ch, ş is a retroflex s, pronounced with the tongue automated download back towards the roof of the mouth, ț is a retroflex t, and ‘ is a glottal stop. Coast Miwok has SVO word order, and resembles Latin in having a system of eight noun cases, marked by suffixes.

sources.note: Title/record only. As a full reconstruction of the Proto-Miwok sound system with daughter-language correspondences it should state the suprasegmental inventory (vowel and consonant length, stress) of each Miwok language including Bodega Miwok; Miwok languages are described without lexical tone, so at most a statement that length and stress, not pitch, are distinctive is expected.
